title: Every RWA structure requires a voter-approved Arranger, and there are currently none
content:
A.3.4.3.1 sets two hard conditions: "Arrangers are directly approved by SKY voters, and all LRA collateral exposure must be structured by an approved Arranger." A.3.4.3 adds that "every Arranged Structure must have a designated Arranger responsible for conducting ongoing reporting." A.3.4.3.2 gives the mechanism — the Core Facilitator may initiate a Governance Poll to onboard or offboard Arrangers, with the roster maintained as an Atlas document.

That document, A.3.4.3.2.1, reads in full: "No current active Arrangers."

Read together with the requirements above, the RWA path is currently gated shut. New Legal Recourse Asset exposure cannot be structured, because there is no approved party permitted to structure it, and existing Arranged Structures cannot have a compliant designated Arranger producing the monthly reporting the Article requires.

This is consistent with the direction of travel elsewhere in the Scope rather than an oversight. A.3.3.2.7.2.1 shows Andromeda — the main legacy RWA arranged structure — non-operational with a zero debt ceiling and being reclassified as a non-ASC asset on transfer to Grove, and A.3.3.2.7.2.2 directs the Core Facilitator to wind down all pre-Endgame legacy RWA when possible. The Arranger framework is being kept in force while the population of Arrangers is empty.

The tension it creates is with the capital framework. The Legal Recourse Asset treatment (A.3.2.2.1.2.4.2) grants an eightfold-plus reduction in measured exposure on the strength of enforceable recourse, and the Basel-based RWA model (A.3.2.2.1.1.1.5) is one of only two fully implemented risk models. Both assume an RWA pipeline that the Arranger requirement currently prevents from operating — and meanwhile named tokenized funds (BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, JAAA) enter the portfolio through the exceptions list rather than through Arranged Structures at all.

The empty list is therefore worth reading as a statement: RWA exposure is presently acquired through tokenized wrappers with administratively assigned capital charges, not through the legally-arranged route this Article describes.
description: All Legal Recourse Asset collateral must be structured by an Arranger directly approved by SKY voters, yet A.3.4.3.2.1 lists 'No current active Arrangers' — closing the route to new LRA exposure.
